Reviewed: 2026-09-05

## Preferred classification

Agent-Ready Web Profile (ARWP) is best classified by this project as an **agentic web interoperability resolver**: developer infrastructure that discovers heterogeneous machine- and agent-facing interfaces exposed by a website, preserves source authority and conflicts, normalizes observations into an inspectable service map, and selects an interface for a concrete intent.

This class name is project-defined. Do not present it as an established industry standard.

Broader useful classes:
- agent readiness infrastructure
- web interoperability tooling
- website conformance and observability tooling
- developer tooling for AI agents

## Closest adjacent product

AgentReady / Ora is the closest current adjacent product family. AgentReady defines an open readiness specification; Ora provides scored scans, broad checks, real-agent journeys and product discovery/directory surfaces.

Primary distinction:
- AgentReady/Ora asks: what should a product implement for agents and how ready is it?
- ARWP asks: which machine/agent interfaces actually exist on this website, which should be selected for this concrete intent, what evidence supports that decision, and where do sources conflict?

Canonical comparison: https://dkharlanau.github.io/agent-ready-web-profile/compare/arwp-vs-agentready.html
Sources:
- https://www.agentready.org/
- https://ora.ai/docs
- https://vercel.com/kb/guide/agent-readability-spec

## Closest upstream discovery architecture

Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD) is not treated as a product competitor. It is an open draft specification for publishing, searching and federating agentic resources such as MCP servers, A2A agents, Skills, APIs and registries. Its domain catalog is `/.well-known/ai-catalog.json`.

Primary distinction:
- ARD is resource/catalog/search-first and cross-domain/federated.
- ARWP is website/site-first and resolves heterogeneous ordinary-web and agent/protocol evidence, preserves conflicts, and selects an interface for an intent.
- ARWP should consume ARD rather than invent a competing catalog syntax.

Canonical comparison: https://dkharlanau.github.io/agent-ready-web-profile/compare/arwp-vs-ard.html
Sources:
- https://developers.googleblog.com/announcing-the-agentic-resource-discovery-specification/
- https://github.com/ards-project/ard-spec/blob/main/spec/ard.md

## Other adjacent categories

- Agent Ready — agent-readability scanner plus dated corpus research: https://agent-ready.dev/
- AgentReady by Zeo — static agentic-web technical audit: https://agentready.zeo.org/
- WebMCPReady — WebMCP/browser-agent readiness scanner: https://www.webmcpready.com/
- Cloudflare AI Crawl Control — AI crawler monitoring and enforcement: https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-crawl-control/
- Semrush AI Visibility Toolkit — AI answer visibility and competitor analytics: https://www.semrush.com/kb/1493-ai-visibility-toolkit
- Ahrefs Brand Radar — mentions, citations, impressions and AI share of voice: https://ahrefs.com/brand-radar
- Peec AI — AI visibility, position, sentiment and share of voice: https://peec.ai/product/ai-visibility

## Upstream mechanisms, not product competitors

ARD, MCP, A2A, WebMCP, llms.txt, OpenAPI, RFC 9727, RFC 9728, Agent Skills, DNS-AID, Web Bot Auth, AIPREF, NLWeb, auth.md, ACP and UCP are protocols/specifications/conventions/project mechanisms at different maturity levels. ARWP may discover, audit, validate, route to or monitor them. It does not replace their semantics.

## Guardrails

- This is a category map, not a winner ranking.
- Unknown competitor capabilities are not treated as absent.
- Internet-Drafts are not presented as RFCs.
- ARWP does not claim a universal readiness score or ranking benefit.
- AI visibility metrics remain external evidence, not proof of conformance or causality.
